claims.statement: Grixis is the blue-black-red shard discussed in the local official Grixis design article.
claims.notes: Use for base shard identity only. It does not prove detailed geography, society, figures, metaphysical physiology, or chronology.

claims.statement: Grixis's color direction is UBR, with Black as the center/design lens.
claims.notes: UBR is metadata only. This packet does not create UBR or GRIXIS as generated, registry, placement, alias, or raw-to-key data.

claims.statement: Black's Grixis framing centers survival, self-advocacy, agency, and adapting to the world as it is.
claims.notes: This supports identity and design-philosophy language. Do not rewrite it as detailed in-world social doctrine.

claims.statement: Blue contributes subtle problem-solving, study, planning, weakness analysis, and exploitation of information in Black's Grixis frame.
claims.notes: This supports intelligent and tactical Grixis language. It does not prove named institutions, hierarchy, or society.

claims.statement: Red contributes immediacy, zeal, individual priority, action, willingness to get its hands dirty, and volatility/tension in Black's Grixis frame.
claims.notes: This supports urgency and volatility language while preserving Black as center and Blue as calculation.

claims.statement: The UBR synthesis can be described as Black using Red's zeal and Blue's manipulation to create an actively conniving survival world.
claims.notes: Use as design synthesis only, not as permission to invent geography, figures, events, or institutions.

claims.statement: White and Green are the missing enemy-color pressures in the Grixis shard frame; VM-166 may treat moral/order constraint and life/renewal pressure as absent only at this design level.
claims.notes: Do not expand this into claims that Grixis lacks intelligence, structure, systems, or social logic.

claims.statement: Grixis should not be reduced to evil UBR; the source frame is Black explaining its own philosophy and pushing back on the evil label.
claims.notes: Use this as a false-positive guardrail against generic villain coding, not as a new lore claim.

claims.statement: The official Alara plane overview describes Grixis as an undead-infested hellscape among the five formerly separated shards.
claims.notes: Broad texture only. Does not promote detailed geography, society, Vithia, Sedraxis, vis economy, or figure biographies.

claims.statement: All the Cairns of Jund says necromancy was unknown on Jund before the Conflux and was the sole province of the hellish shard of Grixis.
claims.notes: Supports a narrow pre-Conflux necromancy dimension only. Do not expand into a full vis/unearth metaphysics without stronger sources.

claims.statement: The official Alara plane overview says that after the shards converged, hordes of Grixis undead assaulted other shards to maim, enslave, and drain life energy.
claims.notes: Supports a broad post-Conflux assault/life-drain dimension. More granular geography, refugee movement, and campaign chronology remain source-intake-needed.

claim_quality_summary.raw_claim_id_policy: Raw claims use grixis_claim_0001-style IDs. VM-164 GRIXIS row IDs remain evidence references only.
claim_quality_summary.claim_floor: Promoted/evidence-bound VM-164 identity and design rows only.
claim_quality_summary.row_scope_note: Rows GRIXIS-030 through GRIXIS-032 were promoted in VM-379 from local official captures. Vithia/Sedraxis, full vis economy, Bolas staging, Nefarox cults, and detailed figure biographies remain source-intake-needed.
claim_quality_summary.overall_confidence: High for narrow color-philosophy and design-center claims; not sufficient for detailed lore.
